title: The Dying Lens Observatory Dilemma

scenario.title: The Dying Lens Observatory Dilemma
scenario.setting: Perched on a wind-scoured western Vermont hill, the Dying Lens Observatory—run by the local amateur astronomy society—sports a rust-fringed metal dome stuck half-open after a late spring ice storm. The society has just 21 days to raise $7,500 to repair the broken dome winch and replace its cracked 12-inch primary mirror, or the county will foreclose and auction the property to a luxury cabin developer. A fledgling GoFundMe campaign has only hit 12% of its fundraising goal so far, with little momentum beyond a small group of dedicated hobbyist members.

characters.name: Marisol Cruz
characters.tendencies: She prioritizes budget spreadsheets, hard donation metrics, and pragmatic cost-cutting over emotional community appeals.

characters.name: Jessa Marlow
characters.tendencies: She focuses on heartfelt personal stargazing stories, rallying local volunteers, and delivering impassioned public pitches to boost donations.

characters.name: Theo Tanner
characters.tendencies: He specializes in troubleshooting vintage electromechanical telescope systems, sourcing used astronomy parts, and walking the society through repair step-by-step.

characters.name: Lila Mae Carter
characters.tendencies: She organizes neighborhood bake sales, coordinates local business sponsorships, and shares the observatory’s plea across community social media groups.

turns.name: Marisol Cruz
turns.text:
I ran the latest donation and expense metrics last night, and our current unrestricted funds only cover about a third of the required repairs to seal the observatory’s wind-damaged siding. We need to pivot from the cutesy community bake sale fundraisers and push for targeted local business grants instead of chasing small, one-off $5 gift donations.
[She flips shut her water-stained budget binder and taps a crumpled repair quote against the frost-fogged pane of the observatory’s entry window.]

turns.name: Jessa Marlow
turns.text:
This wind-scoured Vermont hill has been our amateur astronomy club’s home for 32 years, but our main telescope’s dying lens can barely cut through the hazy twilight to show anyone the crisp rings of Saturn or the glow of the Orion Nebula. We’re calling on local volunteers to help sand and reseal the casing, and small donations to buy a polishing kit to bring the glass back to life for every local kid and stargazer.
[tucking a crumpled handwritten star party flyer behind the handle of a dented telescope tripod propped against the observatory’s weathered wooden wall]

turns.name: Theo Tanner
turns.text:
Easy there, folks—don’t yank that scope’s fine adjustment knob yet, that west wind’s gunning hard for our observatory pier. I grabbed a stack of weatherstripping and a set of aged nylon pulley belts from a closed western Massachusetts observatory last week, just the thing to shore up this old drive train.
[I step over a stack of weathered star charts and twist a rusted lock nut on the mount’s altitude adjustment to test its looseness]

turns.name: Lila Mae Carter
turns.text:
Neighbors hiking this wind-scoured western Vermont hill, stop by our upcoming bake sale at the Dying Lens Observatory parking lot this Saturday. All proceeds will go to fixing our fogged telescope lenses and patching the peeling dome roof, and I’ve lined up a downtown café to sponsor free coffee for everyone who stops by, plus I’ll be sharing every update across our town’s community Facebook groups to spread the word far and wide.
[Kneeling to arrange handwritten price signs for homemade brownies and sugar cookies beside a stack of clear donation jars, while propping a smartphone upright to record a quick Reel for the local community page.]

turns.name: Marisol Cruz
turns.text:
I ran the latest donation and expense metrics last night, and our current unrestricted funds only cover about a third of the required repairs to seal the observatory’s exterior cracks and service the telescope lens. That bake sale will chip away at the gap, but we’ll need to follow up with local small business grant applications rather than relying solely on community bake proceeds to hit our full repair target this quarter.
[She taps a ballpoint pen sharply against the “Repair Fund” line of her dog-eared budget spreadsheet spread across the splintered picnic table beside her.]

turns.name: Jessa Marlow
turns.text:
I still remember the first time a group of local 4-H kids gasped at Jupiter’s moons through that old scope, and that’s exactly the magic we can’t let this wind and broken lens steal. Every dollar from Saturday’s bake sale will go straight to bracing our pier and sealing that lens housing so we can keep sharing this sky for another 32 years. Come by the lot anytime Saturday to grab a treat, learn more about our repairs, or peek through the scope if the clouds clear.
[Adjusting the tattered Dying Lens Observatory banner flapping wildly above her, one frayed edge snagged on a nearby pine branch]

turns.name: Theo Tanner
turns.text:
That’s exactly why I hauled up a stack of weatherstripping and heavy-duty stakes this morning—we can’t touch that dying lens till we shore up the pier and dome against this brutal Vermont wind first. Every penny from Lila’s bake sale will go straight to those emergency repairs, too. No more yanking any fine adjustment knobs till we’ve got this place secured.
[I set a coil of galvanized staples and my rubber head mallet down right next to the observatory’s swaying dome slit.]

turns.name: Lila Mae Carter
turns.text:
Neighbors hiking this wind-scoured western Vermont hill, stop by our upcoming bake sale at the Dying Lens Observatory parking lot this Saturday. All proceeds from every scone, spiced cider, and fudge brownie will go straight to repairing our failing telescope lens and securing our wobbly observatory pier against these brutal gusts. Local shop owners who want to sponsor the event can reach out to me through the county community Facebook group to donate goods or funds.
[Waves a crinkled stack of bake sale flyers to grab the attention of the small group huddled near the telescope’s base before setting a volunteer sign-up sheet on a nearby splintered picnic table.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the Marisol Cruz takes a position; the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Marisol Cruz still holds the line; the next session's hook — a new member, an old scar — is already at the door.
